draft.title: Climate change as a global issue
card: From the 1980s, scientists warned that burning fossil fuels such as coal, oil and gas was adding greenhouse gases to the air. They said this was warming the Earth.
Warming does not stop at borders. Emissions from one country affect the climate of all, so cutting them needs countries to act together.
agreed in 1997. It set emission targets for wealthy countries. Developing countries had no targets.
agreed in 2015. Nearly every country joined, and each set its own goal for cutting emissions. The aim is to limit warming.
draft.remember: Climate change crosses borders, so countries made agreements to cut emissions.

a.q: Why did climate change lead to international agreements?
opts: Emissions affect every country, so action had to be shared
Each country's emissions only harm that country's climate
Scientists had not yet found a link to fossil fuels
Only wealthy countries were producing greenhouse gases
a.why: Greenhouse gases mix in the air and warm the whole Earth, so one country cannot fix the problem alone. Saying the harm stays inside each country is wrong, because emissions affect everyone.
a.clue: Does warming stop at a national border?

b.q: A student says the Paris Agreement was the same as the Kyoto Protocol. Which fact shows the student is wrong?
opts: Paris had nearly all countries set their own emission goals
Paris set targets only for wealthy countries
Paris was agreed before scientists warned of warming
Paris was the first agreement to mention emissions
b.why: Under Paris in 2015, nearly every country set its own goal. Kyoto in 1997 set targets only for wealthy countries. Paris was not the first agreement on emissions, because Kyoto came first.
b.clue: Think about which countries took part in each agreement.

a.best: Emissions affect every country, so action had to be shared

b.best: Paris had nearly all countries set their own emission goals

problems.detail: The clue 'Think about which countries took part in each agreement' implies that only wealthy countries took part in Kyoto. In fact most countries, developing ones included, were parties to Kyoto; the difference was which countries had targets. A better clue would be 'Think about which countries had emission targets under each agreement.'
